question:
Write Sym^n(C^d) for the vectors fixed by every tensor-factor permutation, and q_d(n) for its dimension. (a) For d>=1 and integer n>=0, construct and normalize an occupation-number basis and prove q_d(n)=binom(n+d-1,n) by stars and bars. (b) For fixed d>=2, give the polynomial's exact degree and leading coefficient and prove q_d(n)/d^n->0. State the d=1, n=0 and zero-dimensional boundaries without using a meaningless fraction.

(c) Assess, rather than assume, the assertion that de Finetti/cloning constructions 'live entirely inside Sym^n(C^d)' and that polynomial symmetric dimension alone makes their dimension ratios close to one. Give a permutation-invariant density operator not supported in the original symmetric subspace, and prove that a general permutation-invariant density operator on (C^d)^{tensor n} instead admits a purification in Sym^n(C^d tensor C^d), under the explicit regrouping into n system-reference pairs. Explain the partial-trace route from the pure symmetric de Finetti construction to the mixed one. For fixed d>=1 as m->infinity, determine when q_d(m)/q_d(m+k) tends to one, and exhibit a growing-k regime where it does not; relate this to q_d(N)/q_d(M) for cloning. For the displayed projected cloning core K(X)=[q_d(N)/q_d(M)]Pi_M(X tensor I^{tensor(M-N)})Pi_M, M>=N, distinguish symmetric-input trace preservation and symmetric output support from trace preservation on the full input algebra and from an arbitrary channel completion. Finally explain why a single polynomial-dimensional symmetric block neither replaces all Schur-Weyl blocks in spectrum estimation nor establishes efficient circuit complexity. Retain the original count/asymptotic target; do not salvage(c) by silently assuming original symmetric support.
reference_answer:
(a) Fix a product orthonormal basis e_1,...,e_d. For each tuple f=(f_1,...,f_d) of nonnegative integers with sum n, let W_f be the set of distinct words with those occupations and m_f=|W_f|=n!/product_i(f_i!). The vector |f>=m_f^{-1/2}sum_{w in W_f}|w> has norm one. Different f have disjoint word supports, so these vectors are orthogonal. A vector is fixed by every factor permutation exactly when its coefficients are constant on each word orbit W_f; hence the |f> span the fixed-vector space. Stars and bars counts the tuples as binom(n+d-1,d-1)=binom(n+d-1,n), proving the dimension formula rather than merely citing Weyl.

(b) For fixed d>=1, q_d(n)=product_{j=1}^{d-1}(n+j)/(d-1)! with empty product one. It has degree d-1 and leading coefficient 1/(d-1)!. For d>=2 its ratio to d^n tends to zero: for example the successive-term ratio of q_d(n)/d^n tends to 1/d<1. For d=1 both dimensions are one and the fraction stays one. For n=0 the tensor unit and Sym^0 are C, of dimension one, also when d=0; this is a tensor-unit convention, not a negative-top binomial identity. For d=0,n>0 both spaces have dimension zero and there is no trace-one density operator; the fraction 0/0 is undefined.

(c) Invariant density operators and fixed vectors are different notions. On two qubits put |a>=(|01>-|10>)/sqrt(2). The swap sends |a> to -|a>, so rho=|a><a| is invariant under conjugation by permutations, but Pi_2 rho Pi_2=0. For a genuinely mixed example, I_4/4 is also permutation invariant and has nonzero antisymmetric support. Thus the original blanket support assertion is false, not a consequence of the dimension count.

Here is the actual enlarged-space route, for a nonempty state carrier d>=1. Choose matching product bases on A=(C^d)^{tensor n} and R=(C^d)^{tensor n}, and the UNNORMALIZED maximally entangled vector |Omega>=sum_w |w>_A|w>_R. Define |Psi>=(sqrt(rho) tensor I_R)|Omega>. Its squared norm is tr(rho)=1 and tr_R|Psi><Psi|=rho. If Q_pi rho Q_pi^dagger=rho, spectral functional calculus gives Q_pi sqrt(rho)=sqrt(rho)Q_pi. The permutation matrices are real in the chosen product basis, so (Q_pi tensor Q_pi)|Omega>=|Omega>, and therefore the same simultaneous permutations fix |Psi>. Explicitly reorder A_1...A_n R_1...R_n into (A_1 R_1)...(A_n R_n); this identifies |Psi> with a vector in Sym^n(C^d tensor C^d). Its local dimension is d^2, not d. Applying the pure symmetric de Finetti approximation to the paired systems and tracing each retained reference system gives a mixture of sigma_A^{tensor k} (generally mixed sigma_A), with trace-norm error not increased by partial trace. This uses the pure theorem as an input and the exact purification bridge, not a claim of original-space symmetric support or a new proof of the entire de Finetti theorem.

For fixed d and nonnegative integers m,k,
q_d(m)/q_d(m+k)=product_{j=1}^{d-1}(m+j)/(m+k+j).
For d>=2 and m->infinity, this tends to one precisely when k/m->0. Sufficiency holds factor by factor; conversely the product is at most (m+d-1)/(m+k+d-1), so convergence to one forces k/m->0. If k/m->c in (0,infinity), the limit is (1+c)^{-(d-1)}; if k/m->infinity it is zero. In particular d=2,k=m gives (m+1)/(2m+1)->1/2, despite both dimensions being polynomial. For d=1 the ratio is always one. These are asymptotic statements, not a division-by-m formula at m=0; the exact product remains defined there. Cloning has M=N+k: fixed M-N, or more generally M-N=o(N), gives a ratio tending to one at fixed d, but M/N->c>1 gives c^{-(d-1)}. For the mixed de Finetti route the relevant pure-space dimensions have local parameter d^2. Merely knowing polynomial-versus-exponential growth proves none of these ratio regimes by itself.

For d>=1 and M>=N>=0, let Pi_r denote the symmetric projector. The displayed K is completely positive (tensoring with identity is CP, compression is CP) and every output is supported in Sym^M. To check its actual trace domain, A=tr_{M-N}(Pi_M) is supported in Sym^N because every fully symmetric M-vector is fixed by permutations of its first N factors. A commutes with U^{tensor N}; irreducibility of Sym^N and tr(A)=q_d(M) give A=[q_d(M)/q_d(N)]Pi_N. Hence tr K(X)=tr(Pi_N X), which equals tr X for symmetric-supported inputs and is <=tr X for positive X. K is trace nonincreasing on the full input algebra, not in general trace preserving there. N=M=2,d=2 and the antisymmetric rho above give K(rho)=0 as an explicit failure of full trace preservation.

For any fixed output density sigma, the completion
Ktilde(X)=K(X)+tr[(I-Pi_N)X]sigma
is a CP trace-preserving full channel: the added functional is positive and hence CP, and the trace deficit is exactly supplied. It agrees with K on symmetric-supported inputs. But if sigma is not symmetric-supported and I-Pi_N is nonzero, its full output need not lie in Sym^M. Choosing symmetric-supported sigma gives a completion with symmetric range; the formula and source exercise do not say that every completion, or every arbitrary cloning channel, has that property. When the input already equals its symmetric space (N=0 or1, or d=1), K itself is trace preserving. These formulas are undefined through division by zero on zero-dimensional positive-power spaces and are not asserted there.

Finally, for rho=I_2/2 and n=2, the antisymmetric Schur-Weyl block has probability tr(Pi_anti rho^{tensor2})=1/4. Spectrum estimation therefore cannot discard every nonsymmetric block. Polynomial dimension of the ONE symmetric irrep, the number of all partition labels, and the exponentially large ambient Hilbert-space dimension are different quantities. The count supports structural compression in the stated domains; it is not a gate-count, finite-precision algorithm, or universal implementation theorem.

rubric.criterion: Builds normalized sums over DISTINCT word orbits with m_f=n!/product f_i!, checks orthogonality and spanning of the fixed-vector space, including n=0.

Counts occupations by stars and bars and gives the exact degree d-1/leading coefficient1/(d-1)!; proves the vanishing fraction only at fixed d>=2, and handles d=1, d=0 and tensor-unit boundaries without 0/0 or an invalid binomial formula.

Refutes invariant-density implies original symmetric support; explicitly constructs and normalizes the sqrt(rho) purification, verifies its marginal and simultaneous permutation invariance under paired regrouping, and correctly uses local dimension d^2 and partial-trace contractivity for the mixed de Finetti route.

Derives the exact dimension-ratio product and the fixed-d k=o(m) regime (and counterregime k~m), distinguishes the projected cloner's symmetric input/output and full trace-nonincreasing domain via tr K(X)=tr(Pi_N X), explains a full-channel completion and its possible nonsymmetric output, and does not replace all Schur sectors or infer efficient complexity from one polynomial dimension.

exposition.core_summary: Occupation orbits give the exact symmetric dimension and polynomial/exponential gap. Those facts do not put invariant mixed states in the original symmetric subspace: mixed de Finetti uses paired symmetric purification, while a projected cloning core and its full-channel completion have different support/trace domains.

semantic_steps.claim: Normalized occupation-orbit vectors form an orthonormal basis of the permutation-fixed vector space; conjugation-invariant density operators need not have that support, whereas the explicit paired-system purification does.
Stars and bars gives q_d(n)=binom(n+d-1,n); the exact dimension ratios determine de Finetti/cloning regimes, and the projected cloner has trace tr(Pi_N X) before a full-channel completion.

At fixed d>=2 q_d(n) has degree d-1 and leading coefficient1/(d-1)!, so q_d(n)/d^n vanishes; this alone implies neither arbitrary-support reduction, all-regime ratio closeness nor an efficient implementation, and tensor-unit/zero-space cases remain explicit.
